old_caption: The video captures pretzels suspended in mid-air against a dark background. Several pretzels are visible, varying in shape and size, with some appearing elongated and others more compact. They are positioned above a reflective surface that mirrors their forms. The pretzels remain stationary throughout the sequence, with no motion or descent observed. The lighting highlights their golden-brown color and textured surface. The overall scene is static, with the pretzels maintaining their positions relative to the reflective surface and background.
original_wisa_caption: The video captures a dynamic scene featuring pretzels in mid-air against a dark background. Initially, several pretzels are seen suspended in the air, some appearing to be in motion, possibly thrown or dropped. The pretzels vary in shape and size, with some being elongated and others more compact. As the sequence progresses, the pretzels continue their descent towards a reflective surface below, which mirrors their movement. The lighting is focused on the pretzels, highlighting their texture and color, which is a rich, golden-brown hue. The reflective surface beneath them creates a symmetrical effect, doubling the visual impact of the falling pretzels. The overall atmosphere is one of motion and energy, with the pretzels' descent providing a sense of anticipation and dynamism throughout the video.
caption: The video captures several glossy brown pretzels arranged on a mirror-like gray surface against a dark blue-teal backdrop. On the left, a pretzel tumbles and rotates in place near the surface, its form shifting from an edge-on diagonal bar to a front-facing knot while its reflection mirrors the motion. A short horizontal pretzel rod lies at rest in the center, casting a steady reflection directly beneath it. To the right, a single airborne pretzel spins about a horizontal axis and climbs steadily upward, the gap between it and its reflection widening as it rises. A static pile of pretzels occupies the far-right edge, unchanged throughout. A tiny bright speck drifts faintly near the frame's center. The horizon line and framing remain fixed, holding the scene in a slow, suspended motion.

An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

provided original word count within 85%-115%, using genuinely visible details and process.

the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.
